prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1422; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The insured reported a collision at an intersection while turning left across oncoming traffic, and the claim was opened the same day. The insured is named on the policy, and the policy was in force at the time of loss.

Entry 2: Contact was made with the other driver, who described the crash in the same way the insured did. Both drivers agreed the other vehicle was approaching from the opposite direction.

Entry 3: Two independent witnesses at a nearby business gave statements that match the sequence of events reported by both drivers. Their accounts were taken separately and were consistent with each other.

Entry 4: Scene photographs were received from the insured and show damage to the front of the insured vehicle and the driver side of the other vehicle. The damage pattern lines up with a left turn into the path of the other car.

Entry 5: The insured vehicle was inspected at a repair facility. The damage is consistent with the impact described, and no earlier damage was noted on the vehicle or in prior claim history.

Entry 6: The claimant, who was a passenger in the other vehicle, reported a head injury and was taken to hospital for evaluation. A concussion was diagnosed and the claimant was discharged with follow-up instructions.

Entry 7: The claimant has retained a lawyer, who has asked that all further contact go through that office. Future requests will be sent to counsel.

Entry 8: The claimant described the crash in the same way in each conversation so far, including the initial call and the recorded statement. Medical records show no earlier injury to the same area of the head.

Entry 9: The claimant's treatment has continued for somewhat longer than is typical for a concussion of this kind. The records show ongoing symptom management, and the clinical notes describe the injury as fitting the force of the collision.

Entry 10: It is still not fully clear from the records and photographs where the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the moment of impact. The adjuster has requested seating details and any additional photographs from counsel.

Entry 11: Based on the current file, the reported injury and vehicle damage fit the crash as described, and nothing so far suggests the damage predates coverage. The file will remain open pending the seating information and updated medical records.
